question: Should OpenClaw expose `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate` as a generic OpenAI-compatible configuration and plugin-SDK contract for recognized embedding-model families?
rationale: The implementation is reversible and the default is unchanged, but adding a user-facing boolean and SDK option commits OpenClaw to supporting model-name matching and prompt semantics across generic third-party endpoints; source history only establishes provider-owned behavior for Ollama.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in contract
options.body: Accept the generic configuration direction and retain the focused tests, docs, and default-raw behavior before merging.

options.title: Keep templates provider-owned
options.body: Decline the new generic option and rely on dedicated provider adapters where model prompting is an explicit provider contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Accept the generic configuration direction and retain the focused tests, docs, and default-raw behavior before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory embedding/runtime history and the related custom-endpoint work make this the best available owner for deciding the public configuration boundary.
